'''Bink Otauna''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]]<ref name="TOG" /> who served as a [[lieutenant]]<ref name="Expanded Edition">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story: Expanded Edition]]''</ref> in the [[Galactic Empire]].<ref name="TOG" /> [[Han Solo]] once attempted to befriend both him and [[Tag Greenley]], but eventually determined that the pair was too much of a colossal screwup to be worth hanging around with. Otauna and Greenley were later present during an [[Tribunal of Han Solo|Imperial tribunal]] on [[Carida]] conducted to review Solo's actions during an assault by raiders on [[Onyx Squadron]].<ref name="Expanded Edition" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Tag_and_Bink_HS_Movie.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Howard with Toby Hefferman and Jon Kasdan]]
Bink Otauna was originally a character appearing in the [[Infinities|''Star Wars'' Infinities]] comic series ''[[Star Wars: Tag & Bink]]'', and was created by [[Kevin Rubio]]. [[Toby Hefferman]] portrayed Bink (alongside [[Jon Kasdan]] as Tag) in a [[Content cut from Star Wars|deleted scene]] from the [[2018]] film ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''.<ref name="TagBinkKasdan">{{Twitter|JonKasdan|status/919279777193873408|[[Jon Kasdan]]|quote=Thank You, Kevin. I'm a huge fan and I had to get 'em in there, and then had to play it myself (with Toby Hefferman) to do it justice|archivedate=20190726100746}}</ref> The scene featuring them was cut from the finished version of the film despite Kasdan's objection. They appeared working menial security jobs when [[Han Solo]] was brought before the disciplinary committee at the [[Carida Academy]].<ref name="TagBinkCut">{{Twitter|JonKasdan|status/status/1000608682307010560|[[Jon Kasdan]]|quote=Sadly, #Tag&Bink were left on the cutting room floor despite my strong objection. Look for them in the deleted scenes. They were there, working menial security jobs when Han was brought before the disciplinary committee at the Imperial Academy at Carida.|nobackup=1}}</ref> Although the scene was always present since the film's first screenplay draft, director [[Ron Howard]] was forced to cut the scene because it was deemed unnecessary.<ref name="WhytheCut">{{WebCite|url=https://comicbook.com/starwars/2018/05/26/solo-a-star-wars-story-deleted-scene-tag-and-bink|text=Why Tag and Bink Were Cut from Solo|author=Schmidt, JK|date=2018-05-26|work=ComicBook|archivedate=20181116082332}}</ref>

The [[2018]] [[canon]] reference book, ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]'' by [[Pablo Hidalgo]], confirmed Bink's first and last name.<ref name="TOG" />

''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story: Expanded Edition]]'' by [[Mur Lafferty]] restored the deleted scene from the film, while providing further insights about Solo's previous interactions with the duo.<ref name="Expanded Edition" />
